title: Combining Conditions
description: Combine several conditions in one check using and, or, and not.

content.value: Sometimes a decision depends on more than one thing. You can go to the park only if it is sunny and your homework is done. Python combines conditions with three keywords: `and`, `or`, and `not`. Flip the switches below to see what each one does.

`and` is True only when both sides are True, so a single False makes the whole thing False. `or` is True when at least one side is True, and is False only when both sides are False. `not` takes a single value and flips it to the opposite.

sunny = True
homework_done = True

if sunny and homework_done:
    print("You can go to the park!")

has_cookie = True
has_cake = False

if has_cookie or has_cake:
    print("You have a sweet treat!")
A variable that already holds True or False does not need `== True`. Writing `if sunny:` is the same as `if sunny == True:`, and it reads better.
You can mix these keywords with the comparisons you learned earlier, and combine more than two at once. Use parentheses when you want to be sure which part is worked out first.

age = 15
has_ticket = True

if age >= 12 and has_ticket:
    print("Enjoy the film!")

raining = True
has_umbrella = False

if raining and not has_umbrella:
    print("You will get wet!")

practice.question: Fill in the condition so it prints 'Access Granted!' only when both 'has_key' is True and 'knows_password' is True.
Change the condition so the message prints when the player has EITHER a coin or a ticket.
practice.starterCode:
has_coin = False
has_ticket = True
if has_coin and has_ticket:
    print("You may ride!")

quiz.question: Which operator needs BOTH sides to be True?
quiz.explain: and needs both sides to be True. or needs only one side, and not flips a single value.

quiz.question: If raining = True, what does 'not raining' give you?
quiz.explain: not flips the value. Since raining is True, not raining becomes False.

quiz.question: What is the result of: False or True
quiz.explain: or only needs one side to be True. The right side is True, so the whole thing is True.
